extracted.intended_audience: Researchers (particularly Wellcome-funded) preparing to publish on Wellcome Open Research, and prospective peer reviewers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and standards for participating in Wellcome Open Research's open, post-publication peer review model, covering reviewer selection, reviewer responsibilities and conduct, approval/status criteria, and how authors should respond to reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Openness and transparency of peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer review is fully open: reports are published alongside the article, along with reviewer names and affiliations; open reader commenting is enabled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Making reports and reviewer identities public reduces the possibility of bias, supports constructive reviews, enables collaborative conversation, and provides learning opportunities across the full research community. The model emphasises transparency as central to improving review quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal, invited review process with editorial oversight
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer review is formal and by invitation; all communication with reviewers comes from Wellcome Open Research editorial staff.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial staff manage invitations to maintain integrity of the process. Authors and editors collaborate on reviewer selection, but editorial communications ensure a controlled, consistent invitation process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-publication timing of peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer review is conducted after the article has been published openly on the platform.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publishing first reduces delays so research can be read and used while experts assess it. This balances faster dissemination with later expert validation and enables findings to be available during rapidly changing situations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer assessment focus: quality and validity
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers are asked to assess the quality and validity of the research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessment focuses on whether analysis is accurately presented and conclusions are justified and supported. Null and negative studies are welcomed and reviewed equivalently to positive results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review applies to all article types
rubrics_metrics.description: Open, post-publication peer review is applied to Research Articles and other article types (e.g., Method Articles, Software Tool Articles, Data Notes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures readers can trust underlying work across formats, and that non-traditional outputs receive the same review standards as research articles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author-editor collaboration in reviewer selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors must suggest reviewers and work with the editorial team to identify and approve reviewers rather than editors selecting reviewers alone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should use their subject expertise to suggest appropriate reviewers; editorial team will check suggested reviewers meet criteria and may suggest additional reviewers. Collaboration aims to balance authors' domain knowledge with checks for conflicts of interest and bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authors must suggest five potential reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: After acceptance, authors need to suggest five possible reviewers; the editorial team will check and approve them before publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the suggested names are insufficient or not diverse enough, the editorial team may request additional suggestions. If reviewers decline or miss deadlines, authors and editors will propose more names and repeat invitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer eligibility review / editorial checks
rubrics_metrics.description: Editorial team will check suggested reviewers to ensure they meet Wellcome Open Research's reviewer criteria and Code of Conduct before inviting and before publishing reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reviewers submit reports, editors check reports meet the reviewer Code of Conduct; only then are reports (and reviewer names/affiliations) published alongside the article.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer Code of Conduct compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewer reports must adhere to the platform's reviewer Code of Conduct; reports are checked against this before publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reports failing to meet the Code of Conduct may be blocked or returned; adherence supports constructive, professional, and ethical reviewing. (The page refers to this check but does not reproduce the full Code of Conduct.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Co-reviewing allowed for early career researchers
rubrics_metrics.description: Co-reviewing is offered, where early career researchers can work alongside a more senior researcher to review an article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supports training and inclusion of early career researchers in peer review; co-review arrangements should be declared and follow the platform's reviewer policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approval status definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers assign approval statuses: 'Approved', 'Approved with reservations', or 'Not approved'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approved = appropriate academic standard; analysis accurately presented; conclusions justified and supported; may suggest small changes. Approved with reservations = article has academic merit but requires several small changes or more significant revisions necessary for 'Approved' status. Not approved = issues that seriously undermine findings and conclusions but does not equate to rejection; authors may revise and publish a new version.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review pass thresholds for indexing
rubrics_metrics.description: An article passes peer review and is indexed once it has received two 'Approved' ratings, or one 'Approved' and two 'Approved with reservations'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After meeting the threshold, the article is indexed in industry databases such as Scopus and PubMed. Authors are strongly encouraged to address reviewer feedback by commenting and publishing new versions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance on finding reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Practical tips for identifying potential reviewers: use your knowledge of the field, the Reviewer Finder Tool, look at your references, and search academic databases (e.g., PubMed, Scopus) for recent articles with relevant keywords.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These steps help authors assemble a suitable and relevant reviewer list; editorial staff are available to support if authors struggle to find reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer diversity considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: When suggesting reviewers, authors should consider diversity: different institutions, different countries, and good gender balance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the five suggested names are not diverse enough, the editorial team may request more suggestions. Diverse reviewer pools help mitigate bias and broaden perspectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: How authors should respond to peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should be thorough in responses: address each point in turn and provide a full response, including explanation of any changes made to the paper in light of the comment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed responses build relationships with reviewers/readers, increase transparency, and boost credibility. Authors are encouraged to publish new versions and comment on peer review reports to show how feedback was addressed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authors' right to disagree with reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors do not always need to agree with reviewers and should feel empowered to say no where appropriate, providing a detailed response explaining why and supplying further evidence or explanation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use disagreement as an opportunity to provide more evidence or clarification. Responses should be respectful and evidence-based, maintaining constructive dialogue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expectations about multiple rounds of review
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should be prepared for multiple rounds of review and revisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple rounds are framed as a learning opportunity to improve research and writing; authors should not be disheartened but use rounds to incorporate expert feedback.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintaining integrity through editorial control of invitations
rubrics_metrics.description: All communication with reviewers is managed by editorial staff to maintain integrity of the review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even though authors suggest reviewers, editorial control of invitations and communications reduces risks of bias or impropriety in solicitation of reviews.
